Key Research Thinking Patterns: Tract-Specific Quantitative MRI Biomarker Analysis: Utilizing automated deep learning segmentation (Spinal Cord Toolbox) and Magnetization Transfer Ratio (MTR) to quantify inhomogeneous white matter injury severity in degenerative cervical myelopathy, correlating specific tract deficits (e.g., ventral corticospinal) with clinical mJOA scores.

Interface Engineering for Photovoltaic Stability: Modifying the perovskite/electron transport layer interface using non-fullerene acceptors (Y6-BO/Y7-BO) to passivate surface defects and improve morphology, achieving record power conversion efficiencies (25.82%) and enhanced operational stability in inverted perovskite solar cells.

Transient Cortical Co-Activation Pattern (CAP) Mapping: Deriving millisecond-resolution CAPs from resting-state EEG using k-means clustering on cortical source data to identify recurring neuronal activations that spatially resemble time-averaged resting-state networks, offering higher reproducibility than traditional time-domain measures.

Task-Based Functional MRI for Sensorimotor Pathway Assessment: Employing direct median nerve stimulation as a task-based fMRI paradigm to detect abnormal BOLD signal responses and gray matter recruitment patterns in DCM patients, serving as functional biomarkers for disrupted sensorimotor pathways.
Summary Description: Lei Ding is a biomedical engineer specializing in neuroimaging biomarkers for spinal cord pathology and post-acute COVID-19 cognitive impairment, alongside materials science research for renewable energy. The researcher leverages advanced MRI techniques, including Magnetization Transfer Ratio (MTR) and task-based fMRI with median nerve stimulation, to quantify white matter injury and sensorimotor dysfunction in degenerative cervical myelopathy. Concurrently, they investigate post-COVID brain fog by mapping default mode network connectivity and transient cortical co-activation patterns via EEG. In parallel, Ding applies materials engineering principles to optimize inverted perovskite solar cells, utilizing interface passivation to enhance efficiency and stability. This multidisciplinary profile bridges clinical neurology, computational neuroscience, and solid-state physics to develop diagnostic tools and energy solutions.
